title: A Map of New Beginnings
story:
James sat upon the edge of the heavy oak workbench, the small piece of charcoal held gently between his fingers. The air in the workshop was thick with the scent of lavender oil, hot beeswax, and the steady, comforting tick-tock of a dozen brass clocks. Before him, Barnaby unrolled a large, crackling sheet of heavy cream parchment, smoothing the corners with two polished gear-weights.

Here was the Great Canopy, represented by a few elegant, green-inked swirls at the top left. Here was the open hillside, marked with a single shaded stone. Here was the Whispering Flats, a wide, dusty expanse of pale yellow that led straight to the edge of a dense cluster of tiny black squares. Barnaby tapped the black squares with a weathered finger and spoke a single word: "Oakhaven."

James looked from the map to his own charcoal-stained fingers. With great care, he leaned forward and pressed his charcoal to the parchment, drawing a tiny, slightly crooked circle right on the boulder where his journey had begun. Barnaby watched, his eyes crinkling with a warm, silent approval. The old man then pointed his finger deeper into the heart of Oakhaven, stopping at a grand, domed structure marked with a tiny star—the Grand Library.

With a slow, deliberate movement, Barnaby folded the map into a neat, narrow rectangle, slipped it inside a protective brass canister, and pressed it into James's hands. James held the cool metal tube against his chest, listening to the rain begin to patter softly against the glass. He stared out into the dark, wet streets of Oakhaven, wondering what secrets lay hidden beneath those towering, angled roofs.
